title: Would this inspection model catch rare defects?
scenario: A factory evaluated 20,000 parts, including 200 defective parts. The model predicted every part as acceptable and reports 99% accuracy. Decide whether that evidence supports deployment and select the evidence needed to evaluate the rare defective class.

decisionChoices.label: Approve because accuracy is 99%
decisionChoices.description: Treat overall correctness as sufficient evidence.

decisionChoices.label: Reject the accuracy-only conclusion
decisionChoices.description: Check performance on defective parts and choose a decision threshold based on the cost of missed defects.

decisionChoices.label: Collect only more acceptable parts
decisionChoices.description: Increase the already dominant negative class.

metricChoices.label: Accuracy only
metricChoices.description: Report the fraction of all parts classified correctly.

metricChoices.label: Defect recall and PR-AUC
metricChoices.description: Measure recovered defects and ranking quality relative to the rare-class base rate.

metricChoices.label: Acceptable-part specificity
metricChoices.description: Measure only performance on the dominant class.

evidenceChips.label: The confusion matrix has zero true positives
Defects are only 1% of evaluated parts
